exposure: displacement to Lebanon as Syrian refugees
cohort: The study included 1065 records of Syrian Refugee women, with 634 ever-pregnant women, residing in Lebanon.
finding: After displacement to Lebanon, Syrian Refugee women experienced an increase in C-section deliveries, spontaneous abortions, and maternal complications, alongside a decrease in age at first pregnancy, mean spacing between pregnancies, and breastfeeding rates.
mod_finding: C-section rates were higher among Syrian Refugee women after moving to Lebanon.
